close_reason: Decomposed into children per the bead's own recommendation: .6.1 (handler validation), .6.2 (MemoryBackend filter honoring), .6.3 (integration test for filter + invalidArguments), .6.4 (queryChanges integration test). The fifth recommended child (typed Comparator) is tracked separately at JMAP-ayoz.7. Closing the parent; the children carry the work.
description:
metadata.rs:492-498 and metadata.rs:508-514 delegate Metadata/query and Metadata/queryChanges to jmap_server::handlers::handle_query/handle_query_changes::<Metadata, B>(...). 

Neither has any test in:
- metadata.rs tests module (only /set + /changes are exercised)
- tests/metadata_tests.rs (only all_five_methods_registered checks that the method NAME is registered — it sends a null filter and asserts the response is not 'unknownMethod', but does NOT exercise any filter or sort behavior)

PLAN.md test-cases list (lines 175-189) explicitly mentions:
- Metadata/query: relatedType + relatedIds filter; textMatch filter; combined filters.
- Metadata/queryChanges: standard cycle.

…neither of which is implemented. This is a documented test debt at merge time.

Why this is P1 (correctness-adjacent, not just maintainer-burden):
1. MetadataFilterCondition's relatedIds field has a spec contract — §3.4.1: 'relatedIds MUST only be specified when relatedType is also specified... if relatedIds is specified without relatedType, the server MUST reject the query with an invalidArguments error'. This is wire-protocol-level validation. The generic jmap_server::handlers::handle_query is unaware of this Metadata-specific cross-field constraint — it just parses Filter then hands it to backend.query_objects. So the validation either has to land in the handler shim, in MetadataFilterCondition's Deserialize, or in the backend. Right now it's nowhere.
2. MemoryBackend::query_objects at memory.rs:484-532 IGNORES the filter and sort args entirely (params are _filter, _sort) — returns the entire account's metadata sorted by id. So any Metadata/query call against the reference impl returns garbage. Tests that exercised real filters would surface this.
3. QueryObject::Comparator for Metadata is defined in metadata-types/src/backend.rs:60 as serde_json::Value — not a typed comparator. So sorting is wire-anything-goes. Tests would force this to be honest.

Decompose into 4-5 children:
a) Filter validation: relatedIds-without-relatedType → invalidArguments at the handler shim (NOT the backend) since it's a wire-level cross-field constraint.
b) MemoryBackend::query_objects: actually honor relatedType/@type/isPrivate/relatedIds filters; sort on at least id.
c) Integration test: /query with relatedType filter returns only matching ids; /query with relatedIds without relatedType returns invalidArguments.
d) Integration test: /queryChanges standard cycle (state advances, removed/added correctness).
e) Decide whether Comparator should be a typed enum (issue against metadata-types) — likely follow-up bead, not blocking.

Wire-format correctness gap means this isn't pure maintainer burden — Metadata/query and Metadata/queryChanges currently DO NOT WORK on the reference impl even though they pass dispatch. A consumer wiring the MemoryBackend into a smoke test and calling /query will get plausible-looking-but-wrong data back.
title: Metadata/query and Metadata/queryChanges have NO unit or integration test coverage
